1. port it to the most modern rust gpu and rust 
2. keep the tile renderer its own project independent of Civ3 
3. use the civ3 mod and other tools to get the world state, as well as the camera state from the game. 
4. impl as its own crate a rust-native assert loader for the CIV3 stuff, as well as one to describe how stuff needs to be rendered in toml for stuff that civ3 hardcodes. 
5. combine both to render the world pixel perfect at first:
5a: without UI, cities, borders, units
5b: without UI and units
5c: without UI and unit animations
5d: without UI but not properly working unit animation including when performing actions, including the highlight around the active unit, and including stuff like unit health, movement indicator and country colours
6. impl that in the reimpl renderer keyboard and mouse works
7. impl a rendering system for civ3 menues as another crate and integrate it with the renderer
the end goal here is to have a renderer that is Civ3 unspecific i.e. TileRenderer, and the same for the Menu, independently have asset loaders (reading civ3 assets and toml files), and only have a single crate actually be
Civ3 specific and do the interaction, so that it would be possible to instead drive the renderer with another game that is not Civ3, even while still using Civ3 assests

always use maintainable and safe abstractions. when interopt with unsafe languages create a new crate that creates safe abstractions and use that instead of directly dealing with unsafe code.

if mouse capture is not active the divider between the views has the middle third without the line that separates views visually., so the mouse cannot leave the the view if it moves against the visible separator and does the screen edge scrolling instead. the top left three button are always visible in the active view. where the separator in the middle third is not these the player can move the mouse from one to the other without moving either view. 
Another area where the separators are missing is a bounding box around the unit buttons if they are displayed only, so the mouse can move in there from both screens. 

if mouse capture is on the mouse is printed on both views i.e. for the capture plane dead centre unless edge of map is reached and mouse can be moved (when mouse capture is on the separator in the middle third is also not missing. 

for capture when a new focus of interest appears and smooth scrolling is on, that view used the smooth acceleration that apple uses to pane over to the new location. when mouse capture is on pressing ctrl on its own will release the mouse, and the cursor over the mouse capture panel becomes one that suggests capturing the mouse again. now it can be moved to any UI location. if instead ALT is pressed we enter button snapping mode and the cursor instead snaps to interactable elements by modelling a hidden cursor with momentum and friction originating at the currently snapped location and snapping to the closest element to where the cursor lands with the friction stopping it. this is calculated at 3 times a second (changeable in settings) and the screen visible cursor then moves by the same apple smooth acceleration to the next element so as to it would arrive at the element (i.e. first over flight where it will overrun and then snap back at 133% of the update time i.e. it did not really slow down that much when the next update comes, (only when the cursor animation comes at rest at an element the hoverover for it is shown and it becomes the new origin for momentum calc) i.e. if the at the next update the user moved the cursor more we instead still use the virtual cursor from before and adjust its momentum accordingly to get the new target location to snap to, the animated cursor keeps its current momentum and instead uses the apple smooth acceleration / momentum to be stirred to the new target) - also display a 50% transparent cursor immediately at the target location so its easier to see what is getting targeted. earlier i said the snap target is only updated 3 times per second, however thats for the animated target, the 50% ghost cursor is updated at 30fps) - when in lists the list instead gets smooth scrolled with the cursor staying where it is and it escapes the list when the momentum update lands outside of it.

One problem with the currently published version on my Mac Neo is that the main game menu does not do the same resizing as the other menus. It just stays small and it's always very small. If you have the menu scale to 100%, it should not have any black above or below.

Another thing to add for the menu background: right now what we are doing is discarding, right? An alternative would be that we actually do pixel interpolation for the background if we have to sample it. This makes it an option in the settings menu.

Also by the way, I asked earlier about the Accept and Cancel buttons in the settings. Those already existed. The Accept button is a round button and the Cancel button is an X button. They already existed but now they were replaced with buttons with the text "Accept" and "Cancel". These buttons should be removed. We already have the game buttons. There was nothing needed to replace.
For the preview in the scenario and conquest viewer, currently it's displaying the visible areas of all countries. It should only do that for human-playable countries.

For the preview in the scenario right now, it's not showing anything until all assets are loaded. Previously I explicitly said it should show as soon as possible, but asynchronously in the background. If that means the graphics only switch a bit later because it took some time to load, so be it. That's fine. Also if the units are not there yet because they're not loaded, so be it. That's fine. We just want to see the world as quickly as possible.

Also when I said you can zoom in by double-clicking, what I meant was that it should go to the 2x zoom view, the same one as if you press Z. Right now it's just zooming in by a factor of 2. That's not what I meant. I meant the other direction, like a normal game: press Z, it zooms out once. This is the view that you should get when you double-click.

Another issue in the scenario preview is that right now if you click the up/down button to switch which one it is (or if you click on a scenario with the mouse), it takes quite a while till the menu switches to that entry.
